title: Asbestos communication of hazards, training and housekeeping practice questions
description: Practice questions on asbestos hazard communication: presumed ACM, notices, signs, labels, training and housekeeping (29 CFR 1926.1101(k)-(l)).

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(1)(i), which installed materials must employers and building owners identify as asbestos-containing unless they determine under paragraph (k)(5) that the material is not asbestos-containing?

options.A: TSI and sprayed or troweled on surfacing materials in buildings
options.B: Every ceiling tile in buildings, whatever its installation date
options.C: Only friable materials that are visibly damaged
options.D: Only materials that carry a manufacturer's asbestos label

questions.explanation: The rule says "Employers and building owners shall identify TSI and sprayed or troweled on surfacing materials in buildings as asbestos-containing, unless they determine in compliance with paragraph (k)(5) of this section that the material is not asbestos-containing."

questions.question: A building owner's own records show that a duct sealant, which is not TSI or surfacing material, is asbestos-containing. What does 1926.1101(k)(1)(i) say about such a material?

options.A: It may be treated as non-asbestos because only TSI and surfacing material are presumed
options.B: It is treated as asbestos-containing only if it is friable
options.C: It must be treated as asbestos-containing
options.D: It is treated as asbestos-containing only after a tenant asks

questions.explanation: "If the employer/building owner has actual knowledge, or should have known through the exercise of due diligence, that other materials are asbestos-containing, they too must be treated as such."

questions.question: When owners and employers communicate information to employees under the asbestos standard, how must they identify PACM?

options.A: As "suspect material" until a laboratory reports
options.B: As ACM
options.C: As non-asbestos until tested
options.D: As Class IV material

questions.explanation: The rule says "When communicating information to employees pursuant to this standard, owners and employers shall identify “PACM” as ACM."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(2)(i), what must building and facility owners determine about ACM and/or PACM at the work site before work subject to the standard is begun?

options.A: The manufacturer and installation date of each material
options.B: The airborne fiber concentration in each room
options.C: The disposal site for the material
options.D: The presence, location, and quantity of ACM and/or PACM

questions.explanation: "Before work subject to this standard is begun, building and facility owners shall determine the presence, location, and quantity of ACM and/or PACM at the work site pursuant to paragraph (k)(1)(i) of this section."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(3)(iii), what must the employer whose employees performed the work tell the building/facility owner and employers of employees who will be working in the area within 10 days of completing the work?

options.A: The names of every employee who worked in the area
options.B: The current location and quantity of PACM and/or ACM remaining in the area and final monitoring results, if any
options.C: The total cost of the work
options.D: Each employee's medical examination results

questions.explanation: The employer "shall inform the building/facility owner and employers of employees who will be working in the area of the current location and quantity of PACM and/or ACM remaining in the area and final monitoring results, if any."

questions.question: What time period does 1926.1101(k)(4) set for an employer who discovers ACM and/or PACM on a worksite to convey that information to the owner and to other employers of employees working at the site?

options.A: Within 24 hours of the discovery
options.B: Within 48 hours of the discovery
options.C: Within 72 hours of the discovery
options.D: Within 7 days of the discovery

questions.explanation: All employers who discover ACM and/or PACM "shall convey information concerning the presence, location and quantity of such newly discovered ACM and/or PACM to the owner and to other employers of employees working at the work site, within 24 hours of the discovery."

questions.topic: Showing that PACM is not asbestos
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(5)(ii)(B), who must conduct the tests, evaluation and sample collection used to show that PACM contains no ACM?

options.A: Any competent person on the site
options.B: The building owner's maintenance supervisor
options.C: The employer's foreman
options.D: An accredited inspector or a CIH

questions.explanation: The rule says "The tests, evaluation and sample collection shall be conducted by an accredited inspector or by a CIH."

questions.topic: Showing that PACM is not asbestos
questions.question: A building owner demonstrates that a material presumed to be PACM does not contain asbestos. What does 1926.1101(k)(5)(i) require for the information, data and analysis supporting that determination?

options.A: It shall be posted at the entrance to the area
options.B: It shall be sent to the tenants within 10 days
options.C: It shall be retained pursuant to paragraph (n)
options.D: It shall be kept only until the work is finished

questions.explanation: "However, in all such cases, the information, data and analysis supporting the determination that PACM does not contain asbestos, shall be retained pursuant to paragraph (n) of this section."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(6), where must the building owner post signs that identify the ACM and/or PACM present, its location, and work practices that will ensure it is not disturbed?

options.A: At the entrance to mechanical rooms/areas that employees reasonably can be expected to enter and that contain ACM and/or PACM
options.B: At each elevator lobby on every floor
options.C: At the property line facing the street
options.D: Only in the building owner's office

questions.explanation: "At the entrance to mechanical rooms/areas in which employees reasonably can be expected to enter and which contain ACM and/or PACM, the building owner shall post signs which identify the material which is present, its location, and appropriate work practices" that will ensure it is not disturbed.

questions.question: How does 1926.1101(k)(7)(i) set the distance at which regulated-area warning signs are posted?

options.A: Exactly 10 feet from the regulated area
options.B: Far enough that an employee may read the signs and take necessary protective steps before entering the marked area
options.C: Directly on the regulated area barrier
options.D: At the entrance to the building only

questions.explanation: "Signs shall be posted at such a distance from such a location that an employee may read the signs and take necessary protective steps before entering the area marked by the signs."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(8)(vi)(B), the label provisions of (k)(8)(i) through (iii) do not apply where asbestos is present in a product in concentrations below a threshold. What threshold does the rule set?

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 2.0 percent
options.C: 10 percent
options.D: 1.0 percent

questions.explanation: The label provisions "do not apply where" one listed condition is that "Asbestos is present in a product in concentrations less than 1.0 percent."

questions.question: A building owner's signs at a mechanical room entrance, posted under (k)(6), contain all the information required for labelling. What does 1926.1101(k)(8)(vii) allow?

options.A: The signs replace labels only after OSHA approves them
options.B: Labels must still be fixed to every pipe in the room
options.C: The signs may be posted in lieu of labels
options.D: The signs must be replaced with labels within 30 days

questions.explanation: "Signs required by paragraph (k)(6) of this section may be posted in lieu of labels so long as they contain information required for labelling."

questions.topic: Who is trained and training by class
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(9)(ii), when must asbestos training be provided?

options.A: Prior to or at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter
options.B: Within 30 days after initial assignment and every 3 years
options.C: Once, before initial assignment, with no repeat
options.D: Only when the employee changes employers

questions.explanation: The rule says "Training shall be provided prior to or at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter."

questions.topic: Who is trained and training by class
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(9)(iii), training for Class I operations must be the equivalent in curriculum, training method and length to which training?

options.A: The employer's general Hazard Communication training
options.B: A briefing chosen by the building owner
options.C: The EPA Model Accreditation Plan (MAP) asbestos abatement workers training
options.D: A course of any length chosen by the foreman

questions.explanation: Training for Class I operations "shall be the equivalent in curriculum, training method and length to the EPA Model Accreditation Plan (MAP) asbestos abatement workers training".

questions.topic: Who is trained and training by class
questions.question: An employee does Class II work removing both asbestos containing roofing materials and flooring materials. What training does 1926.1101(k)(9)(iv)(B) require?

options.A: Training only for the category the employee works with most
options.B: Training only for roofing, since it is listed first
options.C: One combined lecture with no category-specific work practices
options.D: Training in the work practices applicable to each category of material removed and each removal method used

questions.explanation: The employee "shall receive training in the work practices applicable to each category of material that the employee removes and each removal method that the employee uses."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(9)(viii), what must each trained employee be informed of about signs and labels?

options.A: The requirements for posting signs and affixing labels and the meaning of the required legends
options.B: The name of the company that printed the signs
options.C: How to order replacement labels
options.D: Only the color scheme of the signs

questions.explanation: Each employee must be informed of "The requirements for posting signs and affixing labels and the meaning of the required legends for such signs and labels."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(k)(10)(i), what must the employer make readily available to affected employees without cost?

options.A: Copies of the employer's insurance policies
options.B: Written materials relating to the employee training program, including a copy of the regulation
options.C: The building's construction drawings
options.D: Purchase receipts for respirators

questions.explanation: "The employer shall make readily available to affected employees without cost, written materials relating to the employee training program, including a copy of this regulation."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(l)(1), where vacuuming methods are selected, what vacuuming equipment must be used?

options.A: Any shop vacuum with a standard dust bag
options.B: Any vacuum, provided it is emptied outdoors
options.C: HEPA filtered vacuuming equipment
options.D: A wet-dry vacuum with no filter

questions.explanation: "Where vacuuming methods are selected, HEPA filtered vacuuming equipment must be used."

questions.question: During interior work that is not a roofing operation, how does 1926.1101(l)(2) require contaminated clothing consigned for disposal to be collected and disposed of?

options.A: Loose in an open-top dumpster
options.B: In sealed, labeled, impermeable bags or other closed, labeled, impermeable containers
options.C: In unlabeled paper bags
options.D: In any trash can emptied at the end of each day

questions.explanation: Asbestos waste and contaminated clothing consigned for disposal "shall be collected and disposed of in sealed, labeled, impermeable bags or other closed, labeled, impermeable containers except in roofing operations", where other procedures apply.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(l)(3)(iii), how must stripping of finishes on vinyl and asphalt flooring material be conducted?

options.A: With high abrasion pads at any speed and dry methods
options.B: By sanding at low speed
options.C: By dry buffing regardless of the finish
options.D: Using low abrasion pads at speeds lower than 300 rpm and wet methods

questions.explanation: "Stripping of finishes shall be conducted using low abrasion pads at speeds lower than 300 rpm and wet methods."
